meta.title: AI Recruiter
meta.description: AI-assisted lead discovery across the public web: criteria in, scored candidates with evidence out.

backend.mockDetail: No external services are called. Every number is fixture data.
backend.unreachableDetail: No answer from {url}. Start it with: docker compose up -d backend
backend.databaseDownDetail: The API is running but PostgreSQL is not answering: docker compose up -d postgres
backend.fixtureDetail: Connected. Search providers are not configured yet, so results come from the seeded catalogue.
backend.readingDetail: Connected. New searches query the live web through {provider} and read the pages they find.
backend.searchOnlyDetail: Connected. New searches query the live web through {provider}; the pages themselves are not read yet.

signalHint.mlm: Partner, distributor or consultant language in public bios
signalHint.beauty: Product category the person actually works in
signalHint.recruiting: Open calls to join a team, posted recently
signalHint.leadership: Mentions of a team, structure or the people they train
signalHint.personalBrand: Own domain, course, podcast or press mentions
signalHint.activity: Posting cadence over the last 30 days

stageNote.generating_queries: Generating search queries from your criteria
stageNote.scoring: Detecting signals and calculating AI scores

unreadable.label: Page would not open
unreadable.hint: The reader failed on the address. Nothing about these people was ever seen.

not_examined.label: Never opened
not_examined.hint: The search already had the leads it was asked for and stopped. Ask for more to reach these.

not_a_profile.label: Not a profile page
not_a_profile.hint: A shop, an article, a login form or a numeric page id — refused for free, before anything was read.

off_source.label: Outside your sources
off_source.hint: Real profiles on a platform you did not pick. Add that platform to the sources to reach them.

not_a_person.label: No person on the page
not_a_person.hint: A brand account, a community or a shop.

wrong_country.label: Another country
wrong_country.hint: The profile places itself somewhere other than the country you asked for.

wrong_language.label: Another language
wrong_language.hint: The profile publishes in a language this search did not ask for.

missing_signals.label: Missing a must-have
missing_signals.hint: Every must-have signal is an AND. Keeping one is usually enough.

unseen.label: Never read
unseen.note: Nobody opened these pages. If a lead was lost, it is here.

excluded.label: Excluded by your sources
excluded.note: Real profiles, on platforms this search was not given.

judged.label: Read and refused
judged.note: The page was opened and failed one of your requirements.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Candidates discovered from public web sources, scored against your criteria.
dashboard.recentSearchesHint: Open a completed search to review its candidates
dashboard.emptyBody: Define who you are looking for and the AI pipeline takes it from there.
dashboard.weeklyAria: Leads discovered per day this week

leads.title: Leads
leads.description: Everything discovered across searches. Status and notes stay with the person, not the search.
leads.emptySavedBody: Use the bookmark in a results table or on a lead page to keep candidates here.
leads.emptyArchivedBody: Archiving hides a candidate from the main list without deleting the evidence.

leadDetail.notFound: This lead could not be found.
leadDetail.whyMatchesHint: Each signal keeps the quote and page it came from
leadDetail.sourcesHint: {count, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} kept for re-analysis
leadDetail.noContacts: No public contact details found. Outreach would go through a platform message.

notes.placeholder: What did you notice about this candidate?

outreach.modalDescription: Generated from the evidence on this profile — review before sending.
outreach.noDraft: No draft yet. Pick a channel and generate one.
outreach.copyFailedBody: Select the text and copy manually.

searches.title: Searches
searches.description: Every search keeps its criteria, so any result set can be re-run or refined later.
searches.emptyBody: Every search starts with criteria: who the person is, where they are, and which signals matter.

progress.notFound: This search could not be found.
progress.pipelineHint: Each step reports from the worker, not the browser
progress.notTakenForwardHint: {count, number} candidates did not meet a requirement

results.noMatchBody: Loosen the score threshold or clear a filter to see the rest of this search.
results.showing: Showing {shown, number} of {total, number} candidates. Duplicates across platforms are already merged into single people.
results.rejectedNote: Every address this search discovered is in one of the two lists, so the pair is the whole of what it saw. A refusal that turns out to be a real person is worth reporting: it is a bug with a URL attached to it.
results.nothingFoundBody: No candidate reached the scoring stage. Widen the keywords or add a source, then run it again.
results.seeEveryFilteredOut: See every candidate that was filtered out
results.nothingFoundIntro: {count, number} candidates were looked at and every one was refused by a requirement. Which requirement, and what to change:

unreadable.label: pages the reader could not open
unreadable.fix: Nothing about these people was ever seen, so this is not a verdict on them. Open the filtered-out list and check the addresses.

offSource.label: offered by the search engine outside your sources, and refused
offSource.fix: Nothing was read or paid for here. If one of your own queries has no site: operator it is asked of the whole web — the wizard now scopes those to the platforms you picked.

notAPerson.label: not people (brand accounts, communities, articles)
notAPerson.fix: Narrow the wording: add a role word to your own query (консультант, дистриб’ютор), or exclude shops with -shop -магазин.

country.label: not confirmed to be in {country}
country.fix: Turn off “only if it can be confirmed” on the Geography step, or put the city into your own query so the description carries it.

language.label: publishing in another language
language.fix: Turn off the language requirement: a two-line profile description often shows no language at all.

signals.label: missing a must-have signal
signals.fix: Keep one must-have. Every extra one is an AND, proven by a quote from a profile that may not have opened.

rejected.nothingTurnedAwayBody: Every candidate this search discovered became a lead. Searches that ran before this list existed show nothing here.
rejected.nothingUnderReasonBody: The counts above cover the whole run; this page of the list does not reach it.
rejected.showingMostPromising: Showing the {shown, number} most promising of {total, number}. The counts above are over the whole run.
rejected.wasRead: The page itself was opened and read.
rejected.wasNotRead: Nobody opened this page — the verdict rests on the search result alone.

descriptions.1: Describe in your own words who you are and who you are looking for. We will turn it into search criteria.
descriptions.2: Fix anything that is off and answer what is missing. Nothing runs until you press the button.

issues.terms: Add a job title, a skill or a brand — how these people describe themselves
issues.sources: Choose at least one source in the advanced settings

geography.noOutsideCountryGeneric: Nobody from outside the chosen country
geography.noOutsideCountryHint: A profile that places the person somewhere else is refused. Turn this off and geographic match goes back to being worth points instead.
geography.confirmedOnly: …and only if it can be confirmed
geography.confirmedLocationHint: Strict: a profile that says nothing about where the person is gets dropped too. Off, it becomes a lead that scores lower — which is usually what you want, because most social profiles never name a city and their pages will not open.
geography.noOtherLanguages: Nobody publishing only in other languages than {languages}
geography.noOtherLanguagesGeneric: Nobody publishing only in other languages
geography.noOtherLanguagesHint: Judged on what the profile is written in.
geography.confirmedLanguageHint: A two-line profile description often shows no language at all. Leave this off unless you would rather have five certain people than fifty likely ones.
geography.socialOnlyWarning: Only social sources are selected. Profiles there rarely state a country or a language, so “only if it can be confirmed” will drop most of what this search finds. Worth turning on once you have seen what it returns without it.

sources.privacyTitle: These are search targets, not logins.
sources.privacyBody: AI Recruiter reads publicly indexed pages only. It never asks for social network passwords, never stores platform cookies and never automates a personal account. Selecting Instagram means “look at public Instagram pages the search engine already indexes”.

review.howMany: How many leads do you want?
review.targetHint: The search stops once it has this many leads that pass every requirement. Candidates are read best first, so what a limit drops is the weakest tail — and the pages it never pays for still become leads from their search result.
review.queryHint: Type the brand people distribute, or how they describe themselves — джерелія, фармасі, консультант. One query is one billed call, and a name your market uses beats any template.
review.queryPickPlace: Pick at least one place to search.
review.queryOwnSite: This query names its own site:, so it is added exactly as written.
review.costBrowserFree: free — Instagram and Facebook are read by our browser
review.costBrowserNote: Instagram and Facebook pages are read by our browser for free; only LinkedIn and other sites are paid pages.
review.costExpectedNote: The expected amount comes from earlier runs: a search stops once it has the leads it was asked for. It will never exceed the ceiling.
review.costFailed: The backend could not price this search. It can still be started — the limits configured on the server apply either way.
review.costTitle: This search will cost at most
review.costPerLead: {pages, number} pages per lead, measured from earlier runs. A page already read this week is free.
review.parsedByRules: The AI is unavailable right now, so the description was read in a simplified way: only the country, languages, well-known brands and the number of leads. Check and complete the fields below.

terms.question: What do these people do, or which companies or brands are they linked to?

sources.question: Where should we look? No source is selected.

country.question: Where should we look? Pick one or more countries, all of Europe, or anywhere. Without a place, queries are written in English only.

languages.question: Which languages do these people write in?

brands.question: Which companies or brands are these people linked to? It is the strongest query — it finds them most precisely.

requirements.question: What makes a candidate right? Add at least one requirement, or every candidate gets the same score.

review.fieldAboutMeHint: Used for outreach drafts. Never part of the search, so it does not find your own team.
review.fieldAboutMePlaceholder: HR at an IT company, Warsaw
review.fieldBrandsHint: Where they work or what they represent. The strongest query: each name is searched on every selected platform. Spell them as profiles do — farmasi and фармасі find different people.
review.fieldKeywordsHint: Words from their profiles: job title, skills, niche. In the language they write in.
review.fieldCountryHint: Pick several countries or all of Europe. Queries are written for each country, and only people from the chosen places become leads.
review.fieldCityHint: Only with a single country. Narrows the search sharply.
review.fieldLanguagesHint: Queries are written in each of these. For a diaspora it is the people's language, not the country's: Ukrainians in Spain write in Ukrainian and Russian.
review.fieldNegativesHint: Pages with these words are dropped before anything is analysed.

warning.confirmed_location_social: Only social sources are selected, and “confirmed only” is on for {country}. Social profiles rarely state a location and their pages often will not open, so most candidates will be dropped as unconfirmed.
warning.confirmed_language_social: “Confirmed languages only” over social sources is strict: a two-line profile description often shows no language at all.
warning.many_must_have: {count} required signals means all of them at once, each proven by a quote from the profile. Two are already hard to find together on a profile that could not be opened.
warning.activity_must_have: “Recent activity” as a requirement gates hard and is worth no points: it needs a date the page states, which a search result usually omits.
warning.no_keywords: No companies or brands, and no words these people use about themselves. Add a job title, a skill or a brand — the way people write it in their profiles.
warning.languages_without_country: Languages are chosen but no country. Queries in languages other than English are written with the place in that language, so without a country none of them will run.
warning.threads_empty: Threads has returned zero results for every query in every measured run, and each one still costs a search call. Unselect it unless you know it works for your market.
warning.city_narrow: A city narrows the queries sharply. If {city} returns little, the country alone usually returns much more.

review.fieldRequirementsHint: Each requirement is checked on the candidate's profile and backed by a quote. You choose how much it matters; the points follow. “Required” drops everyone who does not show it, so one such requirement is best, or none.
review.requirementsEmpty: No requirements yet: every candidate would get the same score.
review.requirementPlaceholder: For example: AWS experience, Speaks Polish…

brief.label: Describe the search in your own words
brief.placeholder: For example: I'm an HR at an IT company in Warsaw. I'm looking for middle or senior Python developers with Django experience who live in Poland…
brief.hint: Write in any language. Brands and the words people use about themselves are kept exactly as you wrote them — those are the search queries.
brief.example: I'm a MIHI leader in Spain. I'm looking for women already working in network marketing in cosmetics — Farmasi, Jerelia — who have their own team or actively invite people. Ukrainian and Russian speakers, in Spain. No shops and no beauty salons. I need 25 leads.

tips.who: Who you are: your brand and role
tips.whom: Who you are looking for: role, skills, what they do
tips.brands: Companies or brands they work with

brief.tooShort: Describe it in a bit more detail — at least one sentence.
brief.failed: Could not read the description. Please try again.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Appearance is yours; provider keys and concurrency limits live on the server and are never sent to the browser.
settings.appearanceHint: Themes are defined as token sets, so new palettes drop in without touching components
settings.autoSaveHighHint: Candidates scoring 90 or above land in Saved leads automatically
settings.notifyDone: Notify me when a search finishes
settings.notifyDoneHint: A toast while the app is open; email once accounts exist
settings.dataSourceMock: The app is running on in-browser fixtures. No search API, scraper or model is called. Switch by setting NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=api once the backend is live.
settings.dataSourceUnreachable: No answer from <url></url>. Start it with <command></command>.
settings.dataSourceDegraded: {service} is up but its database is not answering. Check it with <command></command>.
settings.dataSourceConnected: Connected to {service} v{version} (phase {phase}), storing the workspace in {storage}.
settings.dataSourcePipelineFixture: No external service is called: searches run over the seeded catalogue.
settings.dataSourcePipelinePartial: New searches query the live web; the stages below say what is real and what is still a stand-in.
settings.dataSourcePipelineLive: Every pipeline stage is running against a real provider.

providerRole.postgres: Where searches, leads and notes live
providerRole.redis: Distributed job queue for the workers

adapter.scrapegraph: Opens each candidate page and extracts the profile it states
adapter.llm: Judges each signal on the profile
adapter.snippet: Profiles built from result metadata, not from the page — add SCRAPEGRAPH_API_KEY

settings.readingSourcesHint: Measured from the pages this workspace has opened — not an assumption about the platforms
settings.readingSourcesText: {fallback} A page is read once and reused for {hours, number} hours, so the same profile is never paid for twice.
settings.readingSourcesFailed: The backend did not answer this one.
settings.budgetNote: The wizard sets the target per search and turns it into the budget: <mono>leads × PAGES_PER_LEAD</mono>, capped by the ceiling above. Pages past the budget still become leads — from their search result, at snippet confidence. The credit price is what the plan charges: the API does not report it, so set it from the dashboard.
settings.noPageRead: No page has been read yet.
settings.noPageReadLive: Run a search and this fills in per platform.
settings.noPageReadFixture: Reading starts once SCRAPEGRAPH_API_KEY is set.
settings.resetHint: Clears searches you created, saved flags, statuses and notes
settings.resetModalDescription: Searches you started, saved leads, statuses and notes are removed. Fixture leads come back unchanged.
settings.resetBodyMock: This only touches browser storage — nothing is stored on a server in mock mode.
settings.resetBodyApi: This empties the workspace tables in PostgreSQL and re-applies the seed. Nothing outside this demo is affected.
settings.resetToastBody: Fixtures are back to their original state.
settings.resetFailedBody: The data source did not respond.
